graph_effect.label: No graph finding links area surface temperature to heat ED rates; Madrigano 2015 (literature) links higher surface temperature to heat-wave death in NYC

prediction_scored: miss: the adjusted slope is negative (-10.3% per F, -17.5 to -2.6); unadjusted -6.6% (-13.6 to +1.0). For heat hospitalizations by NTA (HVI file) the adjusted slope is also negative (-3.9%, -7.2 to -0.4).
settle: The cross-sectional association of one afternoon's surface temperature with five-year ED rates is not a dose-response. Hot-surface districts are central (Manhattan, northwest Brooklyn), where residents have lower heat ED rates for reasons the covariates do not capture (age structure is age-adjusted; occupation, housing type, ED access and where people spend hot days are not). Individual-level data linking residence, daily exposure at home and ED visits, or daily ED counts by neighbourhood analysed as a case-crossover with neighbourhood heat as an effect modifier, would settle it.

notes: CDs 101 and 105 have suppressed ED rates; 54 CDs have all covariates. Percent Black is the strongest adjusted predictor of the heat ED rate (+10.9% per 10 points, +1.4 to +21.2). Covariates are unweighted means of NTA values within each CD.
